answer: In PoA, each identity posts bonded collateral in an escrow anchored to an anchor record, so coordinated equivocation by k identities triggers an O(k^2) penalty through pairwise fault attribution. A detected sybil swarm therefore suffers compounding capital loss: the protocol applies an exponential multiplier to forfeitures, rapidly exhausting collateral across linked accounts. This makes jade and juniper identities economically inseparable when they collude, deterring cheap identity proliferation.
